data.long_meaning: One who is always thirsty for knowledge and wisdom, and is constantly seeking it. The name Firasah carries the meaning “Seeker of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Firasah usually hope their child will grow to embody seeker of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom in both the material and spiritual worlds.
data.etymology: Firasah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeker of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Firasah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Firasah holds a deep cultural significance in Islamic tradition as it represents a person who is insatiably curious and eager to acquire knowledge and wisdom. This name is often given to children who are encouraged to explore the world around them and to question the mysteries of the universe. It also reflects the importance of education and learning in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Firasah symbolizes a profound yearning for knowledge and understanding of the divine. It is believed that seeking knowledge and wisdom brings us closer to God and helps us to lead more enlightened and fulfilled lives. By cultivating a thirst for knowledge, we are not only expanding our minds, but also deepening our connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Seeker of Knowledge" symbolizes One who is always thirsty for knowledge and wisdom, and is constantly seeking it.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Firasah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of seeker of knowledge.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, page 335-336. Firasah bint Al-Harith was a queen of the Banu Asad tribe who ruled over Qatif and Bahrain. She converted to Islam and embraced the faith in the presence of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, Period of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's Tarikh Al-Rusul Wa Al- Muluk, Volume 2, page 241-243. Firasah bint Al-Harith was a Yemenite queen who ruled over a part of Yemen during the era of the Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid I. She welcomed the Umayyad army led by Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf and accepted Islam.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate, Expansion of Islam into Yemen
